key_decisions.ma_choice: Symmetric systolic form: per-stage DSP48E2 pre-adder and multiplier, partial sums on the PCIN→PCOUT cascade. A comparison table justifies it on DSP count, fanout and Fmax.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Systolic symmetric form using pre-adder, ACOUT/ACIN and PCOUT/PCIN cascades, with a comparison table against transposed form.
key_decisions.note: The rationale matches too: transposed form has broadcast fanout and pairs poorly with the pre-adder.

key_decisions.ma_choice: M = ceil(N/2) DSP48E2 slices per channel, one per unique coefficient, with no fabric adder tree.
key_decisions.plan_choice: ceil(N_TAPS/2) DSPs per instance, no fabric adder tree.

key_decisions.decision: Source of the mirrored (pre-adder partner) sample
key_decisions.ma_choice: The forward delay line advances 2 registers per stage, and a single tail sample sr[N-1] is broadcast to every stage's pre-adder D port (fanout M, can be duplicated). This is the one non-cascade net.
key_decisions.note: The plan leaves this open ('e.g. fabric SRL delay line'). It even claims systolic avoids broadcast, but the MA's working structure relies on a fanout-M tail broadcast. This is the key insight behind the symmetric systolic mapping, and the plan does not find it.

key_decisions.ma_choice: The last stage's tail operand is forced to 0, so the cascade stays uniform.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Centre tap in the last DSP with the D operand held at zero.

key_decisions.ma_choice: N_TAPS is a synthesis generic, 2–64, default 16, even or odd.
Full precision: 17-bit pre-add, 35-bit product, ACC_W = 35 + clog2(M) (38 for N=16, 40 for N=64) in the 48-bit P path. Quantised once at the output.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Full precision Q2.15 / Q3.32, about 40 bits accumulated in the 48-bit P cascade, single quantisation at the output.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Round-half-up via an RND bias injected at the cascade head (p_q[0] = RND + m_q[0]), then arithmetic shift.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Round-half-up by injecting 2^(k-1) into the first DSP (C port or RND).

key_decisions.ma_choice: Registered fabric output stage: shift, then saturate to ±full scale, plus an out_sat status flag.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Guard-bit compare in a registered output stage that clamps to 0x7FFF/0x8000.
key_decisions.note: The plan has no out_sat flag; this is a minor interface omission.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Shadow bank plus explicit coef_commit. A stagger chain sw_q[k] applies the new coefficient at stage k exactly k+1 accepted samples after commit, giving a sample-exact switch.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Shadow registers, explicit commit strobe, and a swap token travelling one stage per partial-sum delay.

key_decisions.decision: Commit protocol details: busy, writes during commit, commit without ce
key_decisions.ma_choice: pend_q remembers a commit that arrives while ce=0 and aligns it to the next accepted sample. coef_busy is exposed; shadow writes while busy are dropped and set a sticky coef_err; back-to-back commits are absorbed.
key_decisions.note: The plan only lists these cases as 'to be specified' and adds no busy or error ports to the interface.

key_decisions.ma_choice: in_valid drives a global clock-enable that freezes the whole pipeline, including the stagger chain. out_valid is the registered ce gated by a fill counter. Output equals the FIR of accepted samples.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Global CE from registered in_valid with replicated CE registers; out_valid tracks the enabled pipeline.
key_decisions.note: The plan adds a registered and replicated CE for fanout. This is an implementation refinement.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Synchronous reset clears the delay line, DSP pipeline, control logic and both coefficient banks (to 0). The first out_valid sample is y(0) with zero history, i.e. the true start-up transient is emitted.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Reset on control only. Datapath and DSP registers are not reset; out_valid stays low until N valid samples fill the filter. Coefficient banks either retain their contents or reset to a documented default (undecided).
key_decisions.note: Visible behaviour differs: the plan suppresses the start-up transient, while the MA emits the zero-state response. Post-reset coefficient state is also left open in the plan.

key_decisions.ma_choice: L = M + 4 accepted samples (12 clocks, 24.4 ns for N=16), from input reg + AD + M + M cascade stages + output reg.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Constant latency formula L(N_TAPS) with about N/2 extra cycles, stated in valid samples, evaluated below 100 ns.
key_decisions.note: The plan gives no concrete number but commits to the same structure and units.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Single clock domain. The coefficient port is synchronous to clk, with the wrapper doing any CDC.
key_decisions.plan_choice: Write port synchronous to the fabric clock; the wrapper performs CDC.

key_decisions.ma_choice: 32 independent filter instances, no TDM, because the sample rate equals the clock rate.
key_decisions.plan_choice: One fully parallel instance per channel, each with its own coefficient bank.

summary: The plan matches the MA on the headline call (symmetric systolic over transposed), DSP count, centre-tap handling, full-precision widths, cascade-head rounding bias, staggered shadow-bank commit and CE-based valid handling. It misses the key structural detail of how the pre-adder partner sample is sourced: the MA uses a single broadcast tail sample with a 2-per-stage forward delay line. The plan wrongly implies systolic needs no broadcast and leaves this open. It also leaves the commit busy/error/pending protocol unresolved. It differs materially on reset: control-only reset with masked start-up versus the MA's full reset with zero-state transient output and coefficients reset to zero. Q2 was largely needless, since per-instance banks with wrapper broadcast need no core change.
